input.reasoning: Sized backlog using story points where given (mapping ~5-6 team-hours per point, split across roles by task type) and analogy-based sizing for unestimated items relative to comparable estimated ones. Backend gets the largest share given API-heavy scope (auth, payments, RBAC, migration, search, multi-currency). Frontend effort scales with the many customer-facing screens (dashboard, invoices, admin, accessibility, responsive layout). QA (0.6 FTE = ~24hrs/week) is deliberately concentrated on Urgent/High items (auth, payments, RBAC, GDPR, 2FA) since its thin capacity cannot cover full regression on all 24 tasks - this is flagged as a risk. DevOps (0.4 FTE = ~16hrs/week) is scoped tightly to CI/staging setup, observability on the payment path, and legacy decommission, since broader infra work would exceed capacity. Total labour cost forms the base estimate; non-labour covers known third-party/infra costs. Three scenarios reflect uncertainty in unestimated items and risk of thin QA/DevOps capacity causing overruns, particularly on migration and multi-currency work. Reductions target descoping low-value/deferrable items and trimming high-effort medium-priority scope (multi-currency, full accessibility sweep, full-volume migration) to fit tighter budgets without touching Urgent/High priority core functionality.
